note: Re-confirmed 2026-09-08 after the functional-design redo jump. Coverage unchanged.

coverage.target: BR3.2, and functional-spec.md > DateField > 'Primary input: Typing' — AC owned by u7-guest-links; this unit supplies the date field that is fully operable from the keyboard with no picker opened. The range rule itself (AC1.9.2) is explicitly NOT owned here

BR3.5, and functional-spec.md > CopyableValue > 'On success' — AC owned by u7-guest-links; this unit supplies the copy control and a confirmation that is both announced and shown, alongside the value rather than in place of it

BR3.1, and functional-spec.md > CopyableValue > 'Structure' — AC owned by u7-guest-links; enforced here structurally, because the value is always rendered as selectable text and the copy control is only ever an addition
BR2.4, and functional-spec.md > LiveRegion > 'Politeness' — AC owned by u7-guest-links; enforced here by LiveRegion exposing no assertive mode at all, so an assertive announcement is not reachable

BR2.5, and functional-spec.md > Button > 'disabled' — AC owned by u6-owner-locality-billing; this unit makes the disabled reason programmatically reachable rather than adjacent visual text. Which controls are disabled, and why, is that unit's rule
BR3.6, and functional-spec.md > TabBar > 'Keyboard' and 'Selection' — AC owned by u8-guest-app; this unit supplies arrow-key movement between tabs and the invariant that one tab is always selected
BR3.3, and functional-spec.md > TabBar > 'Empty panel' — AC owned by u8-guest-app; this unit guarantees a panel is never silent. The empty-state wording itself is supplied by the consuming unit

BR3.7, and functional-spec.md > Responsive behaviour > TabBar row — AC owned by u8-guest-app; the tab strip scrolls horizontally rather than wrapping or truncating, so every tab stays reachable at the narrowest supported width

reverse.target: boundary rule with no acceptance criterion — it governs what may enter this unit rather than any behaviour a user observes. Its effect is recorded as the eight components this unit does not own (entities.md > 'What this unit does not own'), each with the domain rule that disqualified it

layering rule over theme tokens. Not user-observable; enforced structurally by this unit's dependency set — it cannot reach a locality or a raw visualStyling blob, because u3-foundation owns the only parse (Contract Design C4)

overridability rule over the token categories. Its user-visible effect belongs to NFR3, which cannot be validated inside this unit because brand colours are set after deploy — see functional-spec.md > 'What this unit cannot validate'. Implemented by DesignToken.localityOverridable in entities.md

the default-accessibility rule underlying every AC in the coverage table above, rather than a criterion of its own. Recorded per primitive in functional-spec.md > 'The accessibility contract, per primitive', where six of the nine primitives have nothing overridable at all

the compensating control agreed at this stage's gate for Q1 = A plus Q2 = B. Not user-observable: its effect is that a deviation appears in a diff, which is what makes it reviewable given NFR2's accessibility check is advisory. Exercised by exactly one named override today — Dialog's Escape-closes, taken by u4-owner-shell's SessionExpiredDialog

traces to NFR1's non-colour-dependent status indicators rather than to any single AC, because it applies to every stateful primitive at once. Implemented by StatusBanner's icon-plus-text composition, Button's variant states, and NavRail's programmatic current-item marking (functional-spec.md)

focus-management rule sourced from accessibility-checklist.md, which states it as a standard obligation rather than as a story criterion. Specified as the Dialog state machine in functional-spec.md; its one overridden branch is asserted downstream in u4-owner-shell's session-expired behaviour (AC1.10.3)
